keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row for the Curonians. The page lists the lands (civitates) of Rimbert's Life of Ansgar: Vredecuronia (Vanemane), Wynda (Ventava), Bandowe (Bandava), Bihavelanc (Piemare), Powsare (Duvzare), Megowa, Pilsaten, Ceclis, with Megowa about 500 km2, Pilsaten 200 km2 and Ceclis 1,500 km2; the Courland region plus those three Lithuanian lands is the researcher's reading. 854 is the first dated event on the page (the rebellion against Swedish tribute).

ledger.note: 854: the Curonians refuse Swedish tribute. 'In 854, Curonians rebelled and refused to pay tribute to Sweden.' The lands are older (Rimbert, Life of Ansgar, written before 888; 'Grobin was the main centre during the Vendel Age'); no founding is dated and the Swedish tribute is not drawn as a vassalage.

region.text: northern Courland: Vredecuronia (Vanemane) and the lands of Lammekinus, 'Peace Courland'

ledger.note: 1230: northern Courland makes peace with the Germans. 'In 1230, the Curonians in the northern part of Courland, under their ruler (rex) Lammekinus, signed a peace treaty with the Germans'; the area became Vredecuronia (Peace Courland). Whether the treaty was a conquest or a protection is not on the page; the Brothers of the Sword dossier has Courland conquered in 1230.

ledger.note: 1266: the last Curonian lands are partitioned. 'Curonian resistance ended when all of Courland was partitioned between the Livonian Order and the Archbishop of Riga' (the Curonians page: 'Curonian resistance was finally subdued in 1266'). The page gives no split between the two; the Lithuanian lands of Megowa, Pilsaten and Ceclis are dated by no page and are carried in the same event (confidence 1 for them).

wars.outcome: The Curonians attacked Riga in July 1210 and Daugavgriva in 1228; northern Courland made peace in 1230; the southern Curonians were beaten after Durbe (1260) and Courland was partitioned between the Livonian Order and the Archbishop of Riga in 1266.
wars.note: 1210 is the Curonian attack on Riga (July 1210); the page dates the crusade's start in the 1180s.

certainty.note: Tribal lands; the page gives three areas and the lands' names only. The Courland polygon edges are approximations of the Curonian coast and the Venta.

sources.note: 1210 and 1228 attacks, 1230 peace treaty, Durbe 1260, the 1266 partition between the Order and the Archbishop of Riga.

notes: Not a documented state: tribal lands (the page names the ruler Lammekinus in 1230 and calls a peasant 'the Curonian king' in a later chronicle). Start 854 is the first page-dated event. No capital: the page names Grobin (Grobiņa) only as the main centre 'during the Vendel Age', before the first dated event, so capitals is empty. The page gives no 1267 date (some sources do) and no Baldwin of Alna treaty. The Livonian Brothers of the Sword dossier has Courland conquered in 1230 and Cliopatria draws the Order in Courland from 1227: this dossier keeps the southern lands free to 1266. Archbishop of Riga share (1266) has no dossier. Livonian Coast Curonians in the Lithuanian lands (Megowa, Pilsaten, Ceclis) are dated by no page; those events are confidence 1.
